events.continuity_hook: Starts a larger spring conference episode after the Raleigh work trip wraps and Kara’s April calendar becomes the next planning priority.
events.interaction_goal: Create a practical flight-and-hotel shortlist, compare the conference block against the suite hotel, and identify what the conference office must confirm about presenter setup and Saturday panel timing.
events.scenario_brief: After the Raleigh seminar, Kara is offered a late-April presenter slot at a pediatric rehab conference in Baltimore. She needs to leave Tampa after a Thursday morning virtual class, be near the convention center for a Friday 8:00 a.m. workshop, and stay through a Saturday afternoon panel that may run close to 4:30 p.m. Flight choices split between a Thursday late-afternoon nonstop into BWI and a cheaper one-stop that arrives after 10:00 p.m. The official conference hotel is closest but has limited queen rooms and unclear mini-fridge availability, while a better-rated suite option across the harbor confirms a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room but adds rideshare time.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Baltimore conference planning after the presenter schedule and room-access details make the itinerary ready to book.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the outbound flight, lock the Sunday return, decide whether to stay with the suite hotel, and select a window seat where the seat map allows.
events.scenario_brief: The conference office confirms Kara can access the workshop room Thursday evening and that the Saturday panel should finish by 4:15 p.m. The official hotel block now has only a higher-rate king room with no guaranteed refrigerator, while the suite hotel keeps the queen room and in-room basics available, though it lacks a hot tub. The Thursday nonstop costs more than the one-stop but avoids a late arrival before an early workshop day. Sunday afternoon return flights to Tampa are available, with one mid-afternoon nonstop showing a few window seats.

events.continuity_hook: Revisits the Baltimore lodging choice after a venue-room opening creates a real trade-off between commute convenience and a more predictable room routine.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to switch to the reopened conference hotel room or keep the suite booking before the free-cancel window closes.
events.scenario_brief: Before the suite hotel’s cancellable deadline, the conference block reopens a lower-rate room at the venue. The reopened room would remove the morning rideshare and make it easier to step back between sessions, but it is listed with two double beds, no clear refrigerator, and no recovery amenities beyond a small fitness room. The booked suite still has the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room, but costs more after transportation is included.

events.continuity_hook: Returns to the Baltimore episode after booking, with final conference access instructions driving the last arrival and local-movement decisions.
events.interaction_goal: Set the airport-to-hotel plan, confirm Thursday evening room setup timing, and make sure Sunday checkout and return-flight timing still fit the conference schedule.
events.scenario_brief: About a week before Baltimore, the conference sends final presenter instructions and asks Kara to check in at a side entrance with her demo bag before regular attendee registration opens. Her flights and suite hotel remain in place, with the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room reconfirmed. The unresolved piece is local transportation: light rail from BWI is cheaper but awkward with the demo bag, while rideshare is simpler but may be slower during Thursday evening traffic.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a compact clinic-training episode after the Baltimore conference, as Kara’s May schedule shifts from conference travel back to direct staff coaching.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Madison versus Milwaukee arrival strategies, build a hotel shortlist, and list what the clinic must confirm about Tuesday end time, equipment storage, and parking.
events.scenario_brief: A children’s outpatient therapy practice in Madison asks Kara to run a Monday-Tuesday clinic-training visit in mid-May. She can fly Sunday after a late-morning obligation in Tampa and needs to be at the clinic by 7:15 a.m. Monday. Flights into Madison are limited and mostly connect through weather-prone hubs, while flying into Milwaukee opens better fares but adds a rental-car drive. The closest clinic hotel has mixed recent feedback and no hot tub, though it may have mini-fridges by request; a downtown suite hotel is better rated and lists a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, and fitness room, but it adds a 20-minute morning drive.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Madison clinic-training plan after the host clarifies the schedule and local logistics enough for Kara to commit.
events.interaction_goal: Select the airport routing, choose the hotel, book the return plan around Wednesday afternoon, and secure a window seat if available.
events.scenario_brief: The Madison clinic confirms Kara can store equipment onsite, park near the therapy gym, and finish the Tuesday debrief by 2:30 p.m. Madison flights remain expensive with a late Tuesday return, while the Milwaukee option has a Sunday evening arrival and a Wednesday afternoon return that gives her more breathing room before the next teaching day. The downtown suite hotel confirms the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, and fitness room; the clinic-adjacent hotel still cannot confirm the refrigerator setup and has uneven recent reviews.
